name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.IsIrreducible
title: Nonzero irreducibility without a unit assumption

content.display_title: Nonzero irreducibility without a unit assumption
content.one_sentence_role: Requires nonzero action as well as the absence of proper closed reducing subspaces.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, $H$ a complex Hilbert space, and $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ a $*$-representation. The following predicate defines nonzero irreducibility.
content.definition_explanation: The first condition is $$\exists a\in A:\ \pi(a)\ne0.$$ The second says: for every complex linear subspace $L\subseteq H$ which is closed and satisfies $$\pi(a)x\in L,\qquad\pi(a)^*x\in L\quad(a\in A,\ x\in L),$$ one has $L=0$ or $L=H$. These are the definitions of nonzero action and reduction in [Nonzero action and closed reducing subspaces](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/Representation.lean#L30-L42). Because $\pi(a)^*=\pi(a^*)$ and $A$ is closed under adjoints, invariance under every $\pi(a)$ also gives the stated adjoint invariance; the source records both explicitly.
content.assumptions: No separability or injectivity is assumed. The nonzero requirement is a property of the action $\pi$, not merely of its underlying Hilbert space.
content.conclusion: The zero representation is excluded, and every closed reducing complex subspace is either $0$ or $H$.
